patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch shows a prominent search field in the header with a distinct input box and a separate action area/button on the right.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Should support text entry and search submission, likely via Enter key and clicking the search action area. If implemented like the reference, it may also reveal results on a dedicated search page rather than inline.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not clarify whether results are live/autocomplete or only submitted after activation.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show repeated content/article blocks with a small centered rectangular button inside or beneath preview text, implying actions like 'Read More' or 'Show More' for truncated content.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Buttons should expand preview text or load/open fuller content for each item. The primary top article preview especially suggests progressive disclosure of hidden text.
patterns_found.ambiguities: It is unclear whether each button expands inline, navigates to a full page, or fetches additional content asynchronously.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch has a full-width header/search bar anchored at the very top, visually separated from the content below in a way that commonly implies a persistent top navigation region.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If implemented as sticky, the header/search should remain available during scroll without obscuring content and should preserve keyboard access.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch alone does not explicitly show scrolling states, so persistence on scroll is inferred rather than certain.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The desktop sketch includes an interactive header search control and multiple repeated inline action buttons within content cards, all of which require coherent keyboard focus movement across a dense reading layout.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Programmatic focus handling may be needed if activating 'Read More' expands inline content, updates the DOM, or moves users into newly revealed sections. Search submission and any sticky header behavior should also preserve logical focus order.
patterns_found.ambiguities: No explicit modal/menu/disclosure widget is drawn, so focus management needs depend on whether the buttons expand content inline versus navigate away.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-browsing experience with relatively light JavaScript needs: a strong desktop header search interaction and repeated progressive-disclosure actions for article previews across both viewports. Desktop appears slightly more interactive because of the prominent top search bar and possible persistent header behavior, while mobile is dominated by stacked reading cards with repeated 'read/show more' controls. No clear evidence appears for hamburger navigation, dropdowns, tabs, accordions, modals, or infinite scroll.
